newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Davids to take A$262.4 mln writedown.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Davids to take A$262.4 mln writedown.

text.p: Grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids Ltd said on Wednesday that it would make an abnormal write-down of A$262.4 million as part of a major rationalisation programme.
The company said the abnormal write-down before tax amounted to A$342.64 million but was reduced with the inclusion of a A$80.18 million tax benefit.
It said the write-downs related to goodwill, surplus and non-performing assets and changes in accounting policy.
The rationalisation programme was the result of an examination of operational and financial issues that had arisen from the company's rapid growth over the past three years, it said.
As part of the programme, the board had decided against paying a final dividend for the 1996/97 year ending June 30.
Davids paid a final dividend of five cents per share in 1995/96 based on a net profit of A$51.8 million compared with A$46.3 million a year earlier.
The company said in April that full year earnings would be below the 1995/96 result after abnormal items, citing trading conditions and divisional integration costs.

"When it became clear that we were not going to meet our targets for the year the board began an objective assessment of what is needed to improve our efficiency, lower costs, improve our competitive position and provide more acceptable ongoing return to our shareholders," chairman John David said in a statement.

The company said the after-tax abnormal write-downs consisted of A$45.2 million from changes in accounting policy, A$87.9 million from a business reorganisation, A$119.9 million from devaluation of non-core assets, and A$9.4 million from cost of acquisitions.
It said the business reorganisation included store closures and redundancies, but did not elaborate.
